reviewer.harness: grok-tool-use (GitHub MCP + web + raw.githubusercontent + local file read)

findings.claim: ANCHOR_STALE is documented as 'strict superset; nothing anchored has gone' but the classifier never tests set inclusion, so interior deletions plus net growth are reported as honest growth.
evidence: docs/specs/provenance-anchor.spec.md:157: "`ANCHOR_STALE` | 1 | Store is a strict superset; nothing anchored has gone."

packages/activity_log/anchor.py:393-404: "if vanished or regressions or missing_heads: ... TRUNCATION_DETECTED elif len(leaves) > (anchor.get('packet_count') or 0): ... ANCHOR_STALE else: ... ANCHOR_MISMATCH"
packages/activity_log/tests/test_anchor.py:114-122 only asserts growth-alone is STALE; no test deletes an interior packet and adds two others.
missing_heads iterates only entry.get('head_saids') (anchor.py:389-391), so any non-head SAID can disappear without leaving vanished/regression/missing_heads.
findings.falsifier: A test that deletes an interior packet, adds two new packets, and still returns ANCHOR_MISMATCH or TRUNCATION_DETECTED — or a classifier that checks every anchored SAID (or recomputed leaf set) is still present before emitting STALE.

findings.claim: The specified verify step that walks prev_root is unimplemented, and publish overwrites the only stored anchor document, so the 'anchor series is a hash chain' is a field on the latest file, not a retained series.
evidence: docs/specs/provenance-anchor.spec.md:143: "2. Walk `prev_root` backwards and confirm the series is unbroken."
verify_anchor (anchor.py:327-411) loads one dict, checks its signature, recomputes one root, and classifies; it never opens a previous document or walks prev_root.
scripts/provenance_anchor.py:87-103: previous = load_anchor(args.anchor); then args.anchor.write_bytes(...) to the same DEFAULT_ANCHOR_PATH `.anchors/anchor.json`.
GitHub contents on reconcile/pr38-salvage-20260817: `.anchors/` contains only `anchor.json` (sha f758943a3a5cc3a2d0bfdfae06dcecfdb22175d5).

docs/specs/provenance-anchor.spec.md:111-112: "The anchor series is itself a hash chain via `prev_root`, so dropping an old anchor breaks linkage and is visible rather than silent." Dropping the old file is the default publish path.
findings.falsifier: A `.anchors/` history of signed documents plus verify code that rejects a broken or skipped prev_root against those documents.

findings.claim: The load-bearing publication mechanism (root in a git tag name reaching third-party mirrors) has not been instantiated: the repository has no tags, and the CLI never creates them.
findings.location: scripts/provenance_anchor.py:54-65,118-124; commit fbaae97; GitHub list_tags on G-0-B/FLOSS
evidence: github___list_tags owner=G-0-B repo=FLOSS returned [] — no tags on the public repository.
commit fbaae97b74f72436fe3a79fa792beb4d3eb8ce0e message: "The tag carrying this root is not created here. Pushing a tag to a public repository is an operator action, and the spec says so"
scripts/provenance_anchor.py:118-124 prints `git tag "{tag_name}"` and `git push origin HEAD --tags` only under --print-tag; "Runs none."
tag_name() truncates merkle_root to 24 characters (provenance_anchor.py:64), so even a created tag would not carry the full root the spec treats as the external fact.
docs/specs/provenance-anchor.spec.md:4: "publication ⚠️ not yet performed" and Limits line 209-213 already mark mirror retention Specified.
findings.falsifier: A tag whose name contains the published root, plus a GH Archive / BigQuery row for that CreateEvent on G-0-B/FLOSS retrievable from a party with no write access.

findings.claim: GitHub's public event firehose is a real external record of ref names and commit messages, but it is not a record of the packet set, and this repository's packets are not in the published tree.
evidence: DEFAULT_PROVENANCE_ROOT = WORKSPACE_ROOT / ".agent-surface" / "provenance" (scripts/provenance_anchor.py:47) — parent of the git repo, not inside G-0-B/FLOSS.
.gitattributes marks `.agent-surface/provenance/**/*.json -text` while that path is outside the clone a third party receives.
docs/specs/provenance-anchor.spec.md:145: "3. Independently recompute the root from whatever packet set they hold." A public clone holds `.anchors/anchor.json`, not the 257 packets.
GitHub CreateEvent payload includes `ref` / `ref_type` but not file contents (https://docs.github.com/v3/activity/event_types CreateEvent table).

GH Archive / githubarchive BigQuery retains public PushEvent commit messages and CreateEvent refs (https://trufflesecurity.com/blog/guest-post-how-i-scanned-all-of-github-s-oops-commits-for-leaked-secrets ; https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/optional-skills/security/oss-forensics/references/github-archive-guide.md). That witnesses the string in fbaae97's subject, not the leaf set.
Attempt to list /repos/G-0-B/FLOSS/events returned HTTP 403 rate-limit from this runner — live firehose presence for this repo was not confirmed here.
findings.falsifier: Packets published in-tree (or another public content-addressed store) so a stranger can recompute merkle_root, plus a retrieved GH Archive event whose payload matches that root.

findings.claim: ADR-18 adopt-before-build was skipped for witnessing: Rekor hashedrekord or OpenTimestamps over the already-built root would supply the external 'no-later-than' the git-tag story only Specified, and would not replace the local set-commitment.
findings.location: docs/specs/provenance-anchor.spec.md:219-236 and author's quarantined reasoning; docs/adr/ADR-18-prior-art-reuse-gate.md; Rekor security model
evidence: docs/specs/provenance-anchor.spec.md:223-224: "Rekor becomes a `hashed-rekord` over the same root, at which point a non-operator-controlled Merkle log anchors ours and real inclusion proofs exist." Composition already names Rekor as the witness, then does not call it.
docs/specs/provenance-anchor.spec.md:238-243: prior-art survey was one model family; registry emergency is the admission that reuse review was owed.

Sigstore: "The log is append-only and once entries are added they cannot be modified" and an entry is "a single-party attestation that a piece of data existed prior to a certain time" (https://docs.sigstore.dev/about/security/).
rekor-cli upload of a hashedrekord needs the artifact hash, signature, and public key — the same PyNaCl identity already used (https://docs.sigstore.dev/logging/cli/).

What adopting Rekor/OTS as first witness would lose versus this code: zero-egress offline operation, zero new network dependency, and operator control of when a fact leaves the machine. What it would not lose: leaf format, domain separation, identity summaries, STALE/TRUNCATION split — those stay local.

What a signed git tag alone would lose versus this Merkle document: per-identity max_seq / head_saids / interior_gaps. The custom tree is the set commitment; the tag is only a transport. Building the tree locally is defensible. Treating an uncreated tag as the external root of trust is not.
findings.falsifier: A documented reject of Rekor/OTS that names a concrete property this design needs which those systems cannot carry even as a hash of `.anchors/anchor.json`, or a live Rekor/OTS inclusion proof for the genesis root E3Ehni4XGXL3Zku90BaAfB_HyCOGR4x_cZVCDGTUlYi0.

findings.claim: scan_packets builds interior_gaps with range(max_seq+1) over an unbounded parsed integer, so one packet with a huge `s` wedges or memory-bombs publish/verify.
evidence: anchor.py:193-202: `slot = int(sequence)` with only ValueError handled; no upper bound.
anchor.py:229-244: `top = max(sequences)` then `"interior_gaps": [n for n in range(top + 1) if n not in present]`.
test_anchor.py never uses a large sequence; test_a_packet_with_a_non_integer_sequence_is_named only covers `s="x"`.
findings.falsifier: A rejected or capped sequence in scan_packets, or interior_gaps computed without materialising range(0..max_seq).

findings.claim: publish defaults to load_or_create_identity, so a missing key directory silently mints a new AID and signs a fresh consistent series — the failure mode the spec says pinning exists to stop.
evidence: scripts/provenance_anchor.py:89: `identity = load_or_create_identity(args.identity_dir)` with no confirmation that the AID matches a previous signer.
provenance.py load_or_create_identity: if private.key is absent, `SigningKey.generate()` and write private/public/aid.
docs/specs/provenance-anchor.spec.md:202-204: "A rotated identity can sign a fresh consistent series. Pinning the public key beforehand is the actual root of trust."
verify --expect-signer defaults to None (provenance_anchor.py:143-150), so the minted key verifies against itself.
findings.falsifier: publish refuses to create a key and refuses to sign unless --expect-signer (or a pinned aid file) matches the loaded identity.

findings.claim: The one-line scope 'silent wholesale truncation impossible' is false after the operator publishes a new consistent anchor over the truncated store; verify then returns VERIFIED.
findings.location: packages/activity_log/anchor.py:38-39 and 363-365; accepted limit 1, which is worse than stated once combined with overwrite-publish
evidence: anchor.py:38-39: "this makes silent wholesale truncation impossible and loud truncation attributable, for anyone holding one prior root."
anchor.py:363-365: if current_root == anchored_root: status = VERIFIED — after republish, the truncated store matches the new document.
Accepted weakness 1 says detectability requires a retained prior root; F2 shows the repo keeps only the latest file, so the default verifier holds no prior root.
fbaae97 already published one root in a commit message; a later publish that overwrites `.anchors/anchor.json` and force-pushes the branch leaves only firehose text, not identities[].
findings.falsifier: verify compares the live store to every historically published signed anchor (or refuses VERIFIED when prev_root is not locally present), not only to the overwritten tip file.

findings.claim: Leaf/tree construction (JCS {d,i,s}, 0x00/0x01 domain tags, odd-node promotion, sorted leaves, empty-tree E+43 zeros, sig/signer excluded) is not the exploitable part; no second-preimage or ambiguous packet-set collision is evidenced in the 40-line tree.
evidence: LEAF_TAG = b"\x00"; NODE_TAG = b"\x01" (anchor.py:67-68); interior hash is _hash(NODE_TAG, left, right) (138).
Odd node promoted unchanged (139-140); test_an_odd_leaf_count_is_promoted_not_duplicated asserts merkle_root([a,b,c]) != merkle_root([a,b,c,c]) (test_anchor.py:247-251).
Leaves sorted by (identity, sequence, said) after scan (anchor.py:207).
Empty root is the constant "E"+"0"*43, not blake3(b"") (132-133).
anchor_signing_bytes drops only sig and signer (282-283); test_the_signature_covers_the_identity_summaries tampers max_seq and expects a signature problem (test_anchor.py:188-193).
VerifyKey is derived from signer[1:] (anchor.py:319), so swapping signer without the matching secret fails verification rather than rebinding the claims.
findings.falsifier: Two distinct sorted leaf lists that produce one root under this hasher, or a signature that verifies after identities[] or merkle_root is edited.

findings.claim: Limits section is missing: STALE is not a subset check (F1); prev_root walk is specified and absent (F2); unbounded max_seq materialisation (F6); key auto-mint (F7); packet store is off-repo so public verifiers cannot do spec step 3; operator-republish restores VERIFIED (F8); no concurrent-writer lock around scan-then-sign.
evidence: Limits lists eight items matching the review packet's accepted weaknesses; none mention the STALE heuristic, the single-file overwrite, range(max_seq), load_or_create_identity, or the off-repo store.

scan_packets / build_anchor / sign_anchor / write_bytes is a non-atomic sequence (anchor.py:251-270; provenance_anchor.py:86-103) with no lock on provenance_root; a packet created mid-scan is the accepted window, but a packet half-written then completed can land in unreadable[] or leaves depending on timing, and neither status treats unreadable_now as a failed gate (anchor.py:361 only records it).
docs/specs/provenance-anchor.spec.md:149-150: "Step 4 is the only step that survives an operator who rewrites their own repository." Step 4 has no implementation in verify_anchor or the CLI.
findings.falsifier: Limits rewritten to include each of those behaviours as named, tested properties — or the behaviours changed to match the current Limits text.

findings.claim: This should not be promoted as an external anchor in this form: keep the local set-commitment and identity summaries, stop calling git-tag-as-mirror a witness until one is retrieved, and do not ship STALE as a 'nothing has gone' gate.
evidence: Spec one-liner (215-217) claims silent wholesale truncation is impossible for anyone who has held one prior root.

Shipped surface: one overwritten signed JSON in-tree, packets out-of-tree, zero tags, verify that will VERIFIED a republished truncation and STALE an interior-loss-plus-growth, no Rekor/OTS/SCITT call.

Author's own composition section already splits leaf computation (stable, small, no new dependency) from witnessing (pluggable). The defect is shipping the first half under the threat model of the second.

Genesis commit fbaae97 subject does place root E3Ehni4XGXL3Zku90BaAfB_HyCOGR4x_cZVCDGTUlYi0 and packets=257 in git history — that is a real, weaker, in-band commitment, not the mechanism the spec argues for.
findings.falsifier: A retrieved third-party ingest of the full signed document, STALE defined as actual set inclusion, retained prior anchors, and a pin-required publish path.

predicted_majority: The custom Merkle leaf/tree is acceptable; the publication argument is Specified-not-Verified; ADR-18 should have adopted a transparency log as the witness rather than inventing one from git events; several Limits items are understated.
where_you_expect_to_be_alone: F1 — ANCHOR_STALE as a false-negative classifier for interior deletion plus net growth — because the accepted-weakness list already contains 'window between runs' and 'does not stop the operator', which will absorb this unless someone reads the elif packet_count branch against the spec's 'strict superset' sentence.
